Assignment 5: Cars and Key Fobs
Overview
Almost all cars currently come with a key fob, which allows you to open the doors, and start the car.  When you buy a car, the convenience is the compelling feature.  You can leave the key fob in your pocket, and never again worry about having a physical key. It sounds great.
The implicit assumption you make is that the key fob system is secure, and that some random person with $50 of hardware can't drive off with your car.  You have no real way to tell whether the car company did a reasonable job with their system, so you have to trust them.  Unfortunately, that trust is not always warranted.  And it isn't until people try to hack these systems that the problems come out.  Problems that less scrupulous people may have already been exploiting.
Your Car's Key Fob
There are lots of different key fob systems.  We'll start by looking at the key fob for my 2006 Prius. Key fobs use something called a Remote Keyless System (RKS).  In the U.S. these operate at 315 MHz, +/- 2.5 MHz.  My Prius key turned out to be at 312.590 MHz.The keyfobs are all listed in the FCC database.  Watching for new entries is one of the ways people can tell when new car models are coming out. These will appear long before the official announcement.
You can figure out what frequency your key fob transmits on using your SDR and use GQRX or SDR# to monitor the spectrum.  When you push a button on the fob, you should see a brief jump in the spectrum.  You may need to shift the frequency band up or down by a couple of MHz to find the signal, mine was almost 2.5 MHz low.
One word of caution.  Don't get too carried away pushing the button!  The RKS system uses a rolling pseudo-randomly generated code.  Both the key fob and the car keep in sync, so that the car recognizes the next code.  However, if the key fob gets too far ahead in the sequence (100s of button pushes) the car won't recognize it.  That makes the key (and the car) considerably less useful!
If we capture the signal the result is shown below
The total width of the plot is 10 seconds, so you can see there is one key press shortly after 2 seconds, and another shortly after 5 seconds.
If we plot 100 ms starting at 2 seconds, we can see the digital signal we are looking for:
Zooming in to the first couple of bits, we get
The bits are easy to identify.  A decision threshold of 15 will give almost perfect detection. If we do this, and then plot first part of the digital data for the two key presses, we get this
Although the two start the same, they rapidly diverge.  This is fortunate, because if the signal was the same every time, you'd have enough information to steal my car now!
The data is again on-off keying (OOK).  It is also almost certainly split phase  (or Manchester) encoding. Instead of a “1” being high, and a “0” being low, the information is  encoding in the transition from high to low or low to high. That means that a “0” bit is a rising transition, and a “1” bit is a falling transition.  A good way to recognize split phase encoding is that you can only have one or two low or high segments in a row.  The nice thing about Manchester encoding is that every symbol has a transition, and these are easier to find then when the signal has been high or low for several intervals.
This example is OOK, which is the most common for car remotes.  Some use frequency-shift keying (FSK), where each bit is transmitted as a different frequency, and the envelope is constant.
Attacks on Car Remotes
There are lots of different attacks that can be used against car remotes, depending on how they work, and what sort of access you are looking for.  The simplest just let you open the car up.  More thorough attacks give you complete control by basically cloning the remote.
Most key fobs use a rolling key. This produces a new waveform that depends on the ID of the key fob, a random seed, and how many times the key has been pressed.  The car keeps track of the last code it received, and knows what the next several hundred codes might be.  If it detects one of the expected future codes it opens the car.  If it gets a previously used code, it stops responding to the key fob.  For the Prius you have to do the
“Chicken Dance”
to get it to work again, provided you have another working key fob.  Otherwise, you have to have the dealer rekey the car, for many hundreds of dollars. I have had to do this a couple times, now (for other reasons).
There are several lines of attack.  One is simply recording the key fob output for a couple of button presses when it is away from the car, or the car is being jammed.  With recorded unused codes, you can open the car.
Another is to reverse engineer the RKS sequence.  In general this should be extremely hard.  However, there have been several situations where this is very easy.

这篇文章讨论了汽车 Keyless 系统（RKS）的安全性问题，尤其是钥匙扣的安全漏洞。大多数现代汽车使用钥匙扣来实现无钥匙进入和启动，用户默认信任其安全性。然而，文章指出，一些廉价设备可能破解这些系统，使用户面临风险。钥匙扣通过315 MHz频率传输信号，信号包含滚动码，每次按下按钮时生成新的代码。如果钥匙扣和汽车的代码不同步，汽车将无法识别钥匙扣。

文章详细介绍了如何使用软件定义无线电（SDR）捕捉和分析钥匙扣信号，并指出信号采用OOK（开关键控）和曼彻斯特编码。攻击者可以通过记录信号、重放代码或逆向工程系统来破解钥匙扣。不同车型和系统存在多种攻击方式，有些较为简单，仅需记录按钮按下时的信号，而更复杂的攻击则可能完全克隆遥控。文章还提到，若钥匙扣与汽车失同步，需通过“鸡舞”操作或经销商重新设置来恢复功能。
43780876.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：汽车钥匙（尤其是无钥匙进入和启动系统）的安全性、漏洞、成本以及潜在的解决方案。

不同观点：
• **关于钥匙丢失和成本问题**：
  - mrinterweb 提到 Toyota 车钥匙丢失后，更换和编程费用高达 $550，认为这是垄断性收费，希望能使用更先进的技术如 UWB 来替代现有系统。
  
• **关于 UWB 技术**：
  - sorenjan 引用了 BMW 的 UWB 技术，解释其如何通过测量信号距离来防止中继攻击，认为这是对抗汽车盗窃的有效手段。
  
• **物理屏蔽方法**：
  - myself248 分享了使用物理屏蔽（如铸铁锅）来防止钥匙信号被中继攻击，认为这是简单有效的解决方案。

• **制造商和保险责任**：
  - madphilosopher 认为汽车制造商应为易受攻击车型支付保险费用，因为这些漏洞并非车主所能控制，保险公司因此提高保费是不公平的。

• **传统物理钥匙的弱点**：
  - H8crilA 指出传统物理钥匙容易受到简单的撬锁攻击，虽然有防盗器可以阻止车辆被开走，但仍允许小偷进入车内。

• **替代方案：密码解锁**：
  - 1970-01-01 认为使用密码解锁替代物理钥匙是更安全的选择，尤其是在当前钥匙系统不够安全的情况下。

• **对无钥匙启动系统的质疑**：
  - ta1243 更喜欢使用物理钥匙插入点火开关的方式，认为这样可以明确知道钥匙位置，且需要物理接触才能开走汽车。

• **技术实验与攻击手段**：
  - trishmapow2 提到曾做过关于 RF 干扰和重放攻击的实验，认为低成本的软件定义无线电（SDR）让普通人也能参与这种技术研究。

• **综合防盗系统**：
  - DebtDeflation 提出了一种综合防盗方案，包括 IGLA 系统、隐藏的物理切断开关和 GPS 追踪器，认为这些手段可以有效防止车辆被盗。

• **代码跳跃遥控技术**：
  - Ballas 提到代码跳跃遥控技术早在 20 世纪 80 年代就已存在，对当前系统未采用该技术表示惊讶，并指出虽然代码跳跃系统也有攻击手段，但比现有系统更安全。

• **保险成本的制造商责任实例**：
  - gadders 提到在英国，Range Rover 因为大量车辆被盗，制造商已经开始为车主的保险费用提供补助。

• **UWB 技术的实际应用体验**：
  - crustycoder 分享了自己使用 UWB 钥匙系统的体验，认为该技术已经解决了中继攻击问题，且定位非常准确，需要非常近的距离才能解锁和启动汽车。

• **旧技术的安全性问题**：
  - zero_k 讨论了旧的汽车钥匙加密技术（如 HiTag2 和 Megamos）的脆弱性，认为汽车制造商不应再使用这些技术，并建议使用 AES 加密来提高安全性。

• **简单加密方案的疑惑**：
  - mppm 提出使用简单的加密质询方案（如预共享密钥加上按钮按压）应该可以使钥匙系统非常安全，不理解为何当前未被广泛采用。

• **简单安全方案建议**：
  - bufferoverflow 提出了一个简单的安全协议，基于共享密钥和 SHA256 加密，通过随机挑战数防止重放攻击。

补充讨论：
- 评论中多次提到汽车钥匙系统的漏洞导致车辆被盗问题，并探讨了多种技术解决方案（如 UWB、代码跳跃技术、物理屏蔽等）。
- 保险公司和汽车制造商在处理车辆盗窃风险中的责任也是一个焦点，部分评论者认为制造商应承担更多责任。
- 不同用户提出了不同的技术背景和经验，从简单的物理屏蔽到复杂的加密协议，显示出该问题涉及多方面的技术和经济因素。

主要讨论点：图灵机和数学无穷大概念对有限人类的应用及其哲学讨论

不同观点：
• [meroes的观点] 对图灵机和数学无穷大的实际应用感到困惑。认为图灵机是无限且抽象的，与物理现实无关，但仍然对人类非常有用，这一点让人感到神秘。

• [munchler的观点] 支持Scott Aaronson的演讲，认为演讲内容深刻，难以快速消化。他强调了几点：数学中有限人类试图理解无限；Busy Beaver函数量化了这一点；即使是有限的事物也可能超出宇宙的范围，这时需要物理学和复杂性理论的帮助；量子计算机可能扩展了我们能知道的数学陈述的范围，但最终取决于物理学的终极定律。

• [calf的观点] 对“模拟物理定律”的含义提出质疑，指出常人容易陷入“宇宙是否是计算机”或“无限图灵机与现实世界无关”等混淆的争论。他认为Aaronson的演讲更像是一种哲学立场，而不是严格的论证，并提到有论文批评了计算机科学中对Church-Turing论题等哲学承诺的透明性。他还对演讲中“一页幻灯片证明”的风格表示不满，认为这种风格在认知上对观众是不现实的，除非他们已经了解内容。同时，他提到在理解Busy Beaver函数和Chaitin常数等概念上的新领悟。

补充讨论：
• calf提到对Busy Beaver函数的理解在听完演讲后变得更加清晰，并联想到Chaitin常数和Kolmogorov复杂性，这些概念虽然未在演讲中明确提及，但与之相关。

• 争议的焦点之一在于图灵机和无穷大等抽象概念在现实中的应用及其哲学基础，特别是在计算机科学领域对这些概念的透明性和哲学承诺的讨论。

• 技术演讲的有效性和风格也被提及，calf认为技术演讲有时会因为风格问题而难以跟随，这种现象在专业领域中是公开的秘密。

data.title: Vim Language, Motions, and Modes Explained (2023)
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了Vim编辑器的强大之处，尤其是其独特的快捷键系统（称为Vim语言）和动作模式（motions），这些特性使其在文本编辑中具有极高的效率和定制性。作者比较了其他编辑器如VS Code、Sublime等，认为Vim能够在使用中不断提升速度和效率，且具有精确的文本操作能力。Vim语言类似于一种语法，包含动词（如复制、删除、粘贴等操作）、主体（数字或移动命令）和对象（如特定的寄存器）。尽管初期学习曲线陡峭，但掌握后能极大提升工作效率，且这些快捷方式在其他编辑器和工具中也有应用。作者鼓励所有长时间使用电脑的人学习Vim语言，认为其带来的效率提升和乐趣是值得的。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Vim编辑器的优缺点及其在现代开发环境中的适用性

不同观点：
• **Vim提升效率的看法**：
  - **Palata**：不认为Vim让他比其他人更有效率，因为大部分开发时间并非花在文本编辑上。他使用Vim主要是出于人体工学考虑，减少鼠标使用以缓解手臂疼痛。
  - **Submeta**：虽然Vim的快捷操作很酷，但文本导航并非工程成功的核心因素。现代IDE（如VS Code）能帮助开发者更专注于重要事务，从而提升生产力。

• **Vim的用户体验**：
  - **Gcarvalho**：欣赏Vim没有弹出式干扰，可以直接看到代码，而不被配置和反馈提示打断。
  - **Rgoulter**：提到Helix编辑器，认为其比Vim更直观，具有更好的可发现性和现代特性支持（如LSP、DAP、Tree-Sitter）。

• **Vim的学习与使用难度**：
  - **SaintRomuald**：认为现代IDE的快捷功能和内置特性已非常强大，Vim的键绑定不直观且难以发现新功能，需要主动搜索学习。
  - **Yanis_t**：认为Vim的学习曲线并不陡峭，且其功能比许多人认为的更为强大，特别是在开发环境中的应用。

• **Vim对健康的影响**：
  - **JSR_FDED**：使用Vim完全治愈了他的重复性劳损（RSI）。
  - **NalNezumi**：Vim的键位设计和操作哲学帮助缓解了因鼠标和键盘间切换带来的不适，同时改变了其对工具和编程的思考方式。

• **Vim与其他工具的比较**：
  - **Perizors**：Vim的键绑定对非QWERTY键盘布局不友好，在Colemak布局下使用不便。
  - **Lordleft**：即使不将Vim作为主要工具，学习其键绑定也是值得的，一旦习惯，再也回不去其他编辑器。

• **Vim的创新与教学**：
  - **Nickandbro**：正在开发一个通过游戏化方式帮助用户学习Vim命令的网站，希望能激励更多人学习Vim。

补充讨论：
- **Vim的思维转变**：
  - **NalNezumi**：使用Vim不仅改善了人体工学问题，还改变了其对文本编辑和编程的思维方式，通过宏和交互式操作提升效率。

- **Vim的历史与现代适用性**：
  - **Tdiff**：Vim是特定历史时期的产物，现代终端环境不同，新的教程不断出现以弥合这一差距。

争议焦点：Vim是否在现代开发环境中依然高效，尤其是与现代IDE相比，其键绑定和学习曲线的优劣。

Contents
Why Vim Is More than Just an Editor â Vim Language, Motions, and Modes Explained
Maximizing efficiency and customizability while enjoying editing text.
Data Engineering
2023-01-04
2978 words
14 minutes
Contents
Throughout my time as a developer, I’ve used VS Code, Sublime, Notepad++, TextMate, and others. But shortcuts likeÂ
cmd(+shift)+end
Â and jumping withÂ
option+arrow-keys
Â from word to word needed to be faster at some point.
I was hitting my limits. Everything I was doing I did decently fast, but I didnât get any faster.
I’ve since learned that Vim is the only editor that you get faster using with time.
Vim
Â is based solely on shortcuts. When I discovered that and played around a bit, I felt numb and a little stupid, having not learned the shortcuts (called Vim language) much earlier in my career.
I realized there was a keystroke to get to any specific position I wanted to jump. It was like a game, seeing if I could use fewer shortcuts to accomplish a particular edit. Itâs where many Vim users get a lot of pleasure from coding and writing. It felt liberating, moving my cursor with the precision of a surgeon.
Although speed is a smaller benefit, it got me started when I sawÂ
others
Â navigating in Vim. After climbing the steep learning curve, itâs still one of the most powerful skills I’ve ever learned in my career, working for a living on a computer.
Letâs debunk the myth of Vim and learn how itâs possible to remember all the shortcuts using the specific Vim language. We’ll see how to move with vim motions, and I’ll share what Iâve learned so far, and why you might give Vim a try as well.
Learning the Vim Language
Lots of things have been said about Vim â how fast it is, how only Linux nerds use it, and that itâs impossible toÂ
exit Vim
.
For myself, I fell in love with the âVim languageâ. You see, Iâm bad at remembering anything and thought that Vim was not for me. But this wasn’t the case for one specific reason: VimÂ
motions
Â and its language.
I learned that thereâs a grammar behind the editor. With it, you express what you want to do first, how many times, and then what you want it to apply.
Letâs get deeper into Vim and the language behind it.
How the Vim Language and Motions Work
Vim has a terrific language or grammar behind its shortcuts. Instead of remembering a thousand shortcuts, you can learn a couple and combine them.
These are often called the Vim language or Vim motions for moving around. This has nothing to do with the editor yet â these are universal and available in other editors as well.
For example, there’sÂ
VSVim
Â for VSCode,Â
IdeaVim
Â for the JetBrains products,Â
Vintage Mode
Â for Sublime, and so on. But there are also Browser extensions likeÂ
Vimium
Â orÂ
Firenvim
, and Gmail even adapted some of Vim’sÂ
shortcuts
Â for navigation (
j
,Â
k
Â for moving,Â
g
Â for jumping).
Everyone who types on a computer eight hours a day should learn the Vim language. Yes, itâs hard in the beginning, but thatâs the case with everything new and different. But getting better every day and having more fun coding or writing should be motivation enough. You’re not too busy to learn - you’ll learn as you go.
Are you too busy to improve | Image from
steenschledermann
Vim Grammar
Just as spoken languageÂ
grammar
Â has verbs, subjects, and objects, so does the Vim language. The grammar has differentÂ
verbs
Â to begin with. Copying (or yanking) in Vim withÂ
y
, deleting withÂ
d
, pasting withÂ
p
, changing withÂ
c
, and so on.
For example, the easiest shortcut is copying a line withÂ
yy
. In this case, yank is the verb and the secondÂ
y
Â is a synonym forÂ
y_
. TheÂ
y
Â is doubled up which makes it easier to type since it’s a joint operation.
Next, we can add movements. Each verb takes aÂ
subject
Â for their movements. There are lots of movements (more in the next section) â the easiest is with numbers.
For example, to copy three lines, you add a 3 in front, such asÂ
3yy
. You can do that with all verbs, like deleting three lines isÂ
3dd
. Another would beÂ
{
Â andÂ
}
Â to move to the beginning or end of the paragraph, respectively.
In addition to verbs and subjects, the Vim language also hasÂ
objects
. For example, we can save text into different clipboards (called a register in Vim) withÂ
"ay
. Here, we copy it into register a, which would be the object. We can paste it again by doing the same but using the verb paste instead of yankÂ
"ap
.
There are evenÂ
adjectives
Â andÂ
adverbs
Â with prefixes. Usually, you use a verb and an object. But instead of going down three lines withÂ
3J
, which joins the following three lines, you could addÂ
d5}
, which means âdelete from the current line through the end of the fifth paragraph down from here.â
For me, the most magical thing about Vim is how you navigate and edit text â and it still has nothing to do with the editor.
Sure Vim was the one that introduced and perfected these actions, but again â you can

• **Vim的创新与教学**：
  - **Nickandbro**：正在开发一个通过游戏化方式帮助用户学习Vim命令的网站，希望能激励更多人学习Vim。

data.title: On loyalty to Your Employer
data.author: Peroni
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了对雇主的忠诚问题，特别是科技行业的职业短期性与传统行业中长期雇员的鲜明对比。作者通过其父亲为同一雇主工作30年的例子，指出科技行业员工通常在短时间内频繁跳槽，尽管他们常在社交媒体上赞美雇主。作者是一名招聘人员，提出选择值得效力的雇主的四大标准：合理的薪水、良好的员工待遇、财务稳健和愿意尝试新事物。他强调，雇主并非家人或朋友，员工不应为工作牺牲家庭、心理健康和尊严。尽管工作环境可能看似理想，但员工应保持清醒，认识到自己的可替代性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：雇员与雇主之间的关系，特别是关于忠诚度的理解和职场中的交易性与情感性。

不同观点：
• [rckt, agubelu, bsnnkv, sudofoo, curiousllama, k__] 认为职场关系本质上是交易性的，忠诚度是无意义的。雇员不应期望公司对他们忠诚，公司只在需要时提供回报。忠诚应留给个人关系，而非组织。这种观点强调个人利益和现实，认为对公司忠诚类似于对一台偶尔回报的老虎机忠诚。
  - 例子：rckt分享了他早期职业生涯中意识到公司忠诚度毫无价值的经历。
  - 例子：agubelu指出忠诚适用于家庭和朋友，而非雇主。
  - 例子：k__认为应该忠诚于自己的技能和职业，而非雇主。

• [II2II, runeblaze] 认为虽然职场关系有交易性，但过度强调这种交易性可能对个人和团队产生负面影响。他们建议设定界限，平衡个人和职业生活，同时承认某些职场环境确实存在问题。
  - 例子：II2II指出如果把一切都看作交易，可能会导致负面影响，并强调个人责任。
  - 例子：runeblaze从新毕业生的角度出发，建议不要对自己过于苛责，应把个人幸福放在首位。

• [CharlieDigital, hosh, PeterStuer] 强调生活和工作的平衡，以及在人际关系中寻找价值。他们认为尽管公司可能不忠诚，但在工作中建立的人际网络和关系是有意义的。
  - 例子：CharlieDigital认为生活短暂，应更多关注与亲人和朋友的时光，而非无尽的工作。
  - 例子：hosh指出尽管公司不值得忠诚，但与同事和客户建立的关系是有价值的。
  - 例子：PeterStuer提到公司通过文化和价值观吸引员工，但最终关系仍是交易性的。

• [turtleyacht, vintagedave] 讨论了职场解雇的现实和如何判断公司是否善待员工。他们指出解雇过程的无情，以及从外部判断公司文化的困难。
  - 例子：turtleyacht描述了解雇过程的迅速和无情。
  - 例子：vintagedave质疑Glassdoor等平台的准确性，指出判断公司文化不易。

• [scyzoryk_xyz] 以讽刺口吻总结了对职场忠诚和工作意义的各种矛盾看法，强调不应成为“混蛋”。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于职场忠诚度的意义和价值。一方认为忠诚度在职场中无意义，另一方认为在职场中建立的人际关系值得忠诚。
• 另一个值得注意的点是关于如何判断公司是否善待员工，以及如何从外部评估公司文化。
• 不同代际的视角差异也被提及，新毕业生可能更容易在早期职业生涯中感到忠诚的压力。

43780815.article_content:
On loyalty to your employer
24 Apr
Written By
Stevie Buckley
Note:
This post originally appeared in
HackerNoon
in 2018. I’m republishing it here in order to preserve and share the original piece.
I’ve just returned to London having spent the past two weeks back home in Cork where I spent an awful lot of time with my father, a man who set up his first ever email account less than a year ago and has spent the past 30 years working for the same employer. My Dad is the antithesis of the tech industry in every sense.
Considering the average ‘career’ with each employer in the tech industry is a touch under three years, the idea of spending 30 years working for the same employer is mind boggling. Despite this enormous disparity, I’m constantly witness to colleagues in the tech industry posting on LinkedIn about how great their employer is and why everyone should drop everything and come and work with them, only for them to announce a few short years later that they are moving on “to bigger and better things”.
I’m going to be the first to hold my hands up and admit to being extremely guilty of doing exactly that on a regular basis in the past. I work in recruitment. Employers pay me a lot of money to wax lyrical about how great they are. They pay me to convince you that the grass is not only greener, but their grass is more flexible and inclusive too. So how do I reconcile my apathy towards every employer claiming to be the best, and my ability to do a good job?
Transparency & Honesty
My criteria for vetting an employer worth working with is very straightforward. Anything beyond these four criteria is a bonus (and extremely subjective) but the four criteria below are my absolute zero compromise criteria.
Do you pay reasonable salaries?
Fortunately, due to my line of work, asking for specifics around salaries is par for the course and not something an employer can easily lie about. To put it simply, if your salaries aren’t at least competitive then we’re wasting each other’s time. Pay fairly or pay well and we’re off to a good start.
Do you treat your people well?
Glassdoor is your friend. If there are a slew of negative comments, look for consistencies. Were they all posted around the same time? Are there consistent themes? Raise these points and ask for the employers perspective. A quality employer will be honest and highlight what steps they took to address those issues. Not every company has a helpful Glassdoor profile (a lot of startups have yet to be reviewed) so take to social media, and look up current and former employees to see if there are any red flags.
Are you financially secure?
This is startup 101 folks. Do your due diligence. Companies House, Crunchbase, etc are a good start. Enquire about their runway (how long they can survive if their current income and expenses stay constant). If they aren’t willing to be open and honest about their finances, walk away immediately.
Are you open to trying new things?
This criteria is quite specific to the work I do and may not be universally applicable. If you’re asking me to team up with you to improve your ability to hire people then you categorically need to be open and willing to try new things. No amount of money will be enough to convince me to join your company and follow your same old tired recipe just because it worked well a couple of times in the past.
If you hit all of the above criteria then I can do the thing that enables me to convince great people to work for your company. I can be absolutely transparent and honest with people.
Delicious Kool-Aid
So you’ve landed a great job, the office is incredible, the people seem super friendly, the money is good, the work is challenging and life seems pretty great. Post pictures of your desk littered with company branded swag. Enjoy yourself but don’t delude yourself.
You are a transaction. Sure, your employer gives you the impression they care about you but as soon as you start costing the company money or pose a risk to the company’s image or breach any other element of your 300 page contract, then I can absolutely assure you that they will drop you in a heartbeat. You don’t even need to do anything wrong to be at risk. If the company is struggling financially, due to no fault of yours, you and all your colleagues are at risk. Suddenly the corporate line of “we’re all family here” sounds a bit ridiculous.
Your employer pays you to spend more time with them than you spend with your family and/or loved ones. Your employer is one of the biggest influencers on your mental well-being. Your employer can and will replace you in a heartbeat if absolutely necessary.
Let me be explicitly clear, your employer isn’t your family and they are not your friend. They pay you to do a job and in return your only responsibility is to do that job well.
Do not sacrifice your relationship with family and friends to appease your employer.
Do not sacrifice your mental wellbeing to appease your employer.
Do not sacrifice your dignity

data.title: Someoen accidentally saved half a million-dollars
data.author: jeeybee
data.article_summary: 本文作者讲述了自己意外为公司节省了50万美元的经历，通过简单点击几下按钮解决了持续多年的系统低效问题。公司曾试图建立一个数据分析平台，但由于聘用了大量不合适的顾问和工程师，项目一再拖延，最终演变成一个技术债堆积的混乱系统。作者描述了该系统中的一系列问题，如不必要的复杂数据处理流程、未使用的测试工具和重复的低级代码错误。作者认为，这些问题本应早被发现和解决，但由于管理不善和人员流失，导致了一位员工无辜被解雇。文章批评了公司依赖高薪顾问却忽视实际问题的做法，指出这种行业乱象是造成巨大浪费的根源。

43780520.article_content:
Ludicity
I Accidentally Saved Half A Million Dollars
Published on
October 29, 2023
I saved my company half a million dollars in about five minutes. This is more money than I've made for my employers over the course of my entire career because this industry is a sham. I clicked about five buttons.
Let's talk about why happened and why it's a disgrace that it was even possible.
I. Background
Let's start with some background, because it is fucking
wild
that an inefficiency that took me five minutes to solve in a GUI configuration panel was allowed to persist. We
cancelled someone's contract
the week before I did this.
Someone lost their job
because no one could get their act together long enough to click the button I told them to click.
A few years ago, this company decided that it wanted to create an analytics platform, following the decision to become more "data driven". They hired some incredibly talented people to make this happen, and then like five times as many idiots.
At the time this was happening, I had just graduated and joined the organization as a data scientist. We, of course, did not do any data science, because the organization did not require any data science to be done - what they actually needed to do was fire most of the staff in every team, leaving behind the two people who actually had good domain knowledge, then allow them to collaborate with good engineering teams to build sensible processes and systems. Instead, they hired a bunch of Big Firm Consultants. You can see where this is going already.
Nonetheless, at the time I was young and took the organization at its word. Executives would tell us constantly how excited they were for us to roll out new A.I initiatives (then tell us there was no time, so could we please get that report to them in a spreadsheet), and I'd ask for some sort of compute to
perform
some machine learning, or even set up data pipelines.
It never worked. Instead, we were told that we just had to wait for the Advanced Analytics Platform (AAP) to be deployed. You see, it's December, and it's launching in January.
Then in January I was told to be patient, it was coming in March.
In June, I was told it had been put on hold due to Covid - this was a very convenient excuse because they had absolutely fucked the whole project up already, but it bought some valuable time. By the next December, I had left the organization and the AAP was still nowhere to be seen.
We skip ahead three years. The AAP is finally ready to launch. It turns out none of the features I needed were ever planned, so I guess they were just lying to me before I left.
Four engineers leave the company in the same week, and I speak with the directors because I know they need a
real
engineer in and they can't find them. I'm a substantially less experienced engineer than many of the readers here, but suffice it to say that I can read documentation without panicking, which is considered S-tier in this country. My conditions - a big pile of money and they had to put me on the AAP team because they're the only team that gets actual toys to play with.
II. It Fucking Sucks
It's an insane dumpster fire spiderweb of technical debt and it's only like one week old. Here are some fun details.
I get a friend of mine hired (big fan of nepotism), and he finds,
on day one
, a file in the project's repository that deletes prod using our CI/CD pipelines if it is ever moved into the wrong folder. It comes complete with the key and password required for an admin account. It was produced by the former lead engineer, who has moved on to a new role before his sins catch up with him.
The entire thing is stitched together by spreadsheets that are parsed by Python, dropped into S3, parsed by Lambdas into more S3, the S3 files are picked up by MongoDB, then MongoDB records are passed by another Lambda into S3, the S3 files are pulled into Snowflake via Snowpipe, the new Snowflake data is pivoted by a Javascript stored procedure into a relational format... and that's how you edit someone's database access. That whole process is to upload like a 2KB CSV to a database that has people's database roles in it.
This is considered
more auditable
.

data.title: North American Aviation's 1965 Plan for Piloted Planetary Flybys in the 1970s
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了20世纪60年代美国宇航局（NASA）曾考虑利用阿波罗计划的技术实现载人火星和金星飞越任务的设想。这种飞越任务被视为在阿波罗登月计划后继续探索太阳系行星的最简单方式，宇航员在飞越目标星球后将返回地球。意大利工程师Gaetano Crocco于1956年首次提出这一概念，而NASA自1962年起通过EMPIRE计划开始研究载人飞越任务，目标定于1971年执行首次任务。然而，随着1964-1965年期间总统约翰逊对NASA未来计划的表态，阿波罗计划后的重点转向地球轨道实验室，而非火星或金星飞越。尽管如此，NASA仍继续研究基于阿波罗技术的飞越任务，包括由北美航空公司进行的详细研究。

43780728.article_content:
U.S. President Lyndon Baines Johnson (right) welcomes home astronauts Gus Grissom (center) and John Young (left) after their March 1965 Gemini III test flight. Earth-orbital Gemini was conceived as a means of bridging the yawning gap between "simple" one-man Mercury flights and complex three-man Apollo lunar-orbital and landing missions. Piloted Mars and Venus flybys based on Apollo technology might have played a Gemini-like role in the 1970s NASA program. Image credit: NASA.
A flyby is the simplest planetary exploration mission. We are accustomed today to seeing a flyby as a mission strictly reserved for automated spacecraft. In the early-to-mid 1960s, however, many within the NASA advance planning community believed that piloted flybys based on technology and techniques developed for the Apollo Moon program could enable U.S. astronauts to carry out effective exploration of Mars and Venus as early as the 1970s.
Much like robotic flybys, piloted flybys would limit themselves to small course-correction maneuvers after departing Earth. Robotic flyby spacecraft have no cause to return to Earth after passing their target or targets. Piloted flyby spacecraft, on the other hand, would swing past their target world or worlds on Sun-centered orbital paths that would intersect Earth, enabling their crews to return home.
The piloted flyby concept is usually attributed to Italian aeronautical engineer Gaetano Crocco, who in 1956 presented a paper describing a piloted Mars/Venus flyby. NASA-funded contractor work on piloted flybys began in 1962 with the Early Manned Planetary-Interplanetary Roundtrip Expeditions (EMPIRE) studies at NASA Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC) in Huntsville, Alabama (see "More Information," below). EMPIRE also tasked its contractors with looking at piloted Mars and Venus orbiters.
Crocco and NASA MSFC targeted their first missions for 1971, a date chosen with an eye toward limiting the time and propulsive energy required to reach Mars. In that year, Mars would be close to the Sun as Earth, nearer the Sun and moving faster, passed it. Because Mars has an eccentric orbit, this Earth-Mars geometry recurs only every 15 years or so. An opportunity for an Earth-Mars transfer as favorable would not occur again until 1988.
The piloted flyby mission concept became increasingly attractive during 1964 and early 1965, when U.S. President Lyndon Baines Johnson made clear his vision of NASA's future after the Apollo Program. At that time, Apollo was expected to accomplish its first lunar landing during 1968.
Johnson wanted Apollo lunar exploration to continue after the first successful landing, but mainly he wanted to see astronauts working on board Earth-orbiting laboratories derived from the Apollo spacecraft and Saturn rockets developed for the Moon program. These laboratories would, it was hoped, provide low-cost tangible benefits to American taxpayers through research in the fields of medicine, manufacturing processes, Earth resources discovery, agricultural monitoring, and advanced technology development.
LBJ's vision of NASA's future made no mention of piloted Mars/Venus flybys based on Apollo's technological legacy. On the other hand, neither did it specifically forbid them.
A 15-month NASA MSFC in-house study begun in August 1963, shortly after EMPIRE ended, became, by its end, the first to examine the possibility of adapting Saturn rockets and Apollo spacecraft to piloted Mars and Venus flybys (see "More Information," below). Even before the NASA MSFC engineers completed their study in November 1964, NASA Headquarters and other NASA centers launched their own studies of Apollo-derived piloted flybys. The NASA Manned Spacecraft Center (MSC) in Houston, Texas, for example, completed an in-house study in February 1965.
NASA MSC, which managed the Apollo Command and Service Module (CSM) spacecraft, contracted with North American Aviation (NAA), the CSM prime contractor, for a seven-month piloted flyby study that began on 1 October 1964. MSC then tacked on a two-month extension to NAA's contract so that the company could focus on enhancement of piloted flyby spacecraft long-term reliability through use of in-flight maintenance. NAA briefed MSC management on the results of its study in Houston on 18 June 1965.
The NAA study was significant in the evolution of piloted flyby planning because it was the first conducted by a major manufacturer of prospective piloted flyby hardware. In addition to the CSM, NAA was responsible for other Apollo hardware that might be adapted to a piloted flyby mission; specifically the Spacecraft-Launch Adapter (SLA) and the Saturn V rocket S-II second stage.

data.title: Give People Something to Look At (2021)
data.author: thisismytest
data.article_summary: 作者发现，当人们参与活动或有东西可看时，交流变得更加轻松。例如，走路、开车或玩游戏时，人们不必直接对视，从而减少了对反应的过度分析，对话中的停顿也显得自然。作者认为，缺少可注视的对象时，人们会更在意对视和反应，导致尴尬。在工作中，作者通过让面试候选人或会议参与者注视白板或屏幕上的笔记，成功缓解了紧张氛围，使交流更加顺畅。因此，提供一个可注视的对象是促进轻松对话的有效方法。

43781031.article_content:
30 Oct 2021
•
communication
A long time ago, I realized that some of my easiest conversations were while walking or hiking or driving in a car with someone. Then I noticed that group chats were much easier when the group was playing a game. People can go from anxious small talk to conversing like old friends after 5 minutes of poker.
For a long time I thought that the key element to this increased ease came from having an activity to do or a shared interest to discuss. People relax when they can socialize on top of something with more rigid expectations and rules. People bond over shared interests.  But in recent years I’ve realized that there’s something else at play. I think a key element to the increased ease is that people have something to look at - the path ahead, the road, the gameboard.
Without something to look at, people have to look at the each other. With that comes a lot of subconscious (and conscious) reading into reactions. Pauses in the conversation are awkward because you’re just staring at each other.
However, with something to look at, there’s less overanalyzing. Conversations can have pauses more naturally because you’re contemplating the thing in focus, instead of staring in expectation.
I think this is part of why, for example, people walking dogs often have more conversational ease - the dog gives something for prospective chatters to direct their gaze towards. I think this is why bars with sports on TV are often less awkward. I’ve had many great conversations while staring at sports I cared nothing about.
I started testing this hypothesis at work and the outcomes validated it in dramatic fashion.
Now, instead of slightly awkward interviews staring at candidates, I try to always have one person writing on a whiteboard. Instead of having group meetings where each person gets a spotlight of focus each time they talk, I always present notes on the screen. It’s amazing how that simple change can make a hot-topic meeting go from feeling like a battle royale to a less anxious, more collaborative effort.
I also present notes I’m taking in every one-on-one that I do. Beyond giving people something to focus on, it also has the benefit of making sure good and accurate notes are taken.
In life and at work: if you’re looking for a shortcut to relaxed conversation, give people something to look at.

data.title: Reptends and Reciprocals
data.author: pavel_lishin
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了某些整数的倒数在特定进制下具有重复的、包含所有数字的特性，称为“非冗余全数字 reptends”。例如，在十进制中，整数 72,728 的倒数 1/72,728 的十进制表示有一个长度为 10 的重复块，包含从 0 到 9 的所有数字。类似地，文章列举了不同进制下具有这种特性的最小整数及其倒数的重复块。例如，在二进制中，1/3 的倒数是 0.(01)，在六进制中，1/93 的倒数是 0.(021534) 等。这些整数在特定进制下具有全数字且非冗余的重复块，展示了数学中数的奇妙对称性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国长除法的记法是否合理及其对学习难度的影响

不同观点：
• Joker_vD认为美国的长除法记法不直观且复杂。他们指出，将除数放在被除数的左边，并将答案写在顶部是不自然的，主张采用更直观的"被除数 / 除数"顺序，并将答案写在右边。例如，1 / 28 = 0.03571428...。这种记法更符合逻辑顺序，减少了不必要的步骤和混淆。
• 另一种观点（隐含在Joker_vD的评论中）可能认为现有的记法虽然初看反常，但可能有其历史或教学上的原因。尽管Joker_vD强烈批评，但也提到"这可能更糟"，暗示现有的方法虽然复杂，但还不是最差的。

补充讨论：
• Joker_vD提到长除法本身已经是最复杂的算术算法之一，而多余的记法 convolutions 只会让事情更复杂。他们认为初始步骤中交换数字的位置是完全不必要的，这增加了学生的困惑。
• Joker_vD还提到了一种更极端的记法——“galley division method”，暗示尽管现有方法不理想，但还有更不寻常的记法存在，这可能为现有方法提供了一些对比和背景。
• 争议的焦点在于记法的直观性与复杂性。批评者认为不必要的复杂性增加了学习难度，而可能存在的支持者则认为现有方法可能有其特定的教育价值或历史背景。

43767910.article_summary: 文章探讨了某些整数的倒数在特定进制下具有重复的、包含所有数字的特性，称为“非冗余全数字 reptends”。例如，在十进制中，整数 72,728 的倒数 1/72,728 的十进制表示有一个长度为 10 的重复块，包含从 0 到 9 的所有数字。类似地，文章列举了不同进制下具有这种特性的最小整数及其倒数的重复块。例如，在二进制中，1/3 的倒数是 0.(01)，在六进制中，1/93 的倒数是 0.(021534) 等。这些整数在特定进制下具有全数字且非冗余的重复块，展示了数学中数的奇妙对称性。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows系统中任务栏和开始菜单的附加功能（如广告、秒数显示等）对能源消耗的影响以及用户体验

不同观点：
• whoisthemachine认为，虽然节省能源是一个值得尊重的目标，但在任务栏和开始菜单中加载广告或进行频繁的截图等操作所消耗的能源可能微乎其微。他质疑这种做法对整体能源节省的实际效果，暗示这种做法可能没有抓住重点。

• firstordefault则关注用户体验方面，提到自己在任务栏上显示秒数已经很多年，甚至忘记了这是由"7+ Taskbar Tweaker"添加的功能，而不是Windows的原生功能。这表明某些用户可能已经习惯了这些附加功能，并且对其存在没有明显的不满或察觉。

补充讨论：
• whoisthemachine提出的能源消耗问题可能涉及更广泛的讨论，即操作系统中的非核心功能（如广告加载、自动截图等）是否真的对设备性能和能源使用产生显著影响。

• firstordefault的评论则反映了用户对某些定制功能的依赖和习惯性，可能意味着微软或其他软件开发者在移除或修改这些功能时需要考虑用户的实际使用体验和习惯。

• 争议的焦点可能在于，用户对任务栏或开始菜单中附加功能的实际需求和其对系统资源（包括能源）的潜在影响之间如何平衡。这涉及到软件设计中的功能取舍和用户体验优化问题。

data.title: Ofcom announces new rules for tech firms to keep children safe online
data.author: beardyw
data.article_summary: Ofcom宣布了新的网络安全规定，要求科技公司在2025年7月前采取措施，阻止儿童访问有害内容，否则将面临巨额罚款甚至被关闭。这些措施包括更严格的年龄验证、过滤有害内容的算法、快速删除危险内容以及简化投诉系统。尤其是大型社交媒体平台将受到严格监管，涉及暴力、仇恨、虐待、网络欺凌、自杀、自残和色情等内容必须彻底屏蔽。科技部长Peter Kyle考虑引入社交媒体宵禁，并认为Ofcom的新规应成为改变在线有害环境的转折点。然而，网络安全活动人士Ian Russell认为这些措施不够有力，无法有效防止更多悲剧发生。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在线平台应如何管理和限制有害内容的传播，以及是否应为成年人和儿童设置不同的内容访问规则。

不同观点：
• Spivak认为，有害内容（如暴力、仇恨、虐待、网络欺凌等）应被平台限制传播，尤其是涉及自杀、自残、饮食失调及色情内容应完全屏蔽在儿童接触范围之外。他质疑，为何这些保护措施仅限于儿童，而成年人不应同样受到保护。他建议，可以对所有用户默认应用类似电影分级的系统（G、PG、R），并允许父母通过家长控制进行管理，而不是通过年龄验证系统来区分。

• 隐含观点是，支持对所有用户（包括成年人）实施内容保护措施，而不是仅限于儿童。Spivak质疑为何成年人应被区别对待，暗示成年人也应获得同样的内容保护。这里的论据是，有害内容对任何人都有潜在危害，因此不应只保护儿童。

• 另一种观点是，支持现行的分级制度，默认对未成年人实施更严格的限制，但对成年人开放访问权限。此观点可能认为成年人有能力判断并处理他们接触到的内容，因此不需要像保护儿童一样保护成年人。这一观点隐含了对个人自由和责任的强调，认为成年人应有权选择他们想要接触的内容。

补充讨论：
• Spivak提到，如果对所有用户都实施同样的内容限制，就不需要复杂的年龄验证系统，这可以简化平台的管理和用户的访问体验。

• 争议的焦点在于，是否应为成年人和儿童设置不同的内容访问规则，以及如何在保护用户和尊重个人自由之间取得平衡。Spivak的建议倾向于更统一的保护措施，而另一种观点则支持更分级化的管理方式。

43780426.article_content:
Ofcom’s ‘children’s codes’ require sites to have easier complaints systems to help users flag harmful content more quickly.
Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA
View image in fullscreen
Ofcom’s ‘children’s codes’ require sites to have easier complaints systems to help users flag harmful content more quickly.
Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA
Internet safety
Ofcom announces new rules for tech firms to keep children safe online
Companies will be legally required to block children’s access to harmful content under UK’s Online Safety Act or face large fines
UK politics live – latest updates
Dan Milmo
Global technology editor
Thu 24 Apr 2025 03.02 EDT
First published on Thu 24 Apr 2025 02.15 EDT
Share
Social media and other internet platforms will be legally required to block children’s access to harmful content from July or face large fines, Ofcom has announced.
Tech firms will have to apply the measures by 25 July or risk fines – and in extreme cases being shut down – under the UK’s
Online Safety Act
.
The communications watchdog published more than 40 measures on Monday covering sites and apps used by children, ranging from social media to search and gaming.
Under the measures,
the “riskiest” services
, which include big social media platforms, must use “highly effective” age checks to identify under-18 users; algorithms, which recommend content to users, must filter out harmful material; all sites and apps must have procedures for taking down dangerous content quickly; and children must have a “straightforward” way to report content.
Melanie Dawes, Ofcom’s chief executive, said
the changes were a “reset”
for children online and that companies failing to act would face enforcement.
“They will mean safer social media feeds with less harmful and dangerous content, protections from being contacted by strangers and effective age checks on adult content,” she said.
The measures were published as the technology secretary, Peter Kyle, said he was considering a social media curfew for children after TikTok’s introduction of a feature that encourages under-16s to switch off the app after 10pm.
Kyle told the Telegraph he was “watching very carefully” the impact of the wind-down feature.
“These are things I am looking at. I’m not going to act on something that will have a profound impact on every single child in the country without making sure that the evidence supports it – but I am investing in [researching] the evidence,” he said.
Kyle added on Thursday that the new
Ofcom
codes should be a “watershed moment” that turned the tide on “toxic experiences on these platforms”.
“Growing up in the digital age should mean children can reap the immense benefits of the online world safely, but in recent years too many young people have been exposed to lawless, poisonous environments online which we know can lead to real and sometimes fatal consequences. This cannot continue,” he added.
Online platforms will be required to suppress the spread of harmful content, such as violent, hateful or abusive material and online bullying. More seriously harmful content, including that relating to suicide, self-harm and eating disorders, will need to be kept off children’s feeds entirely, as will pornography.

The online safety campaigner Ian Russell, whose 14-year-old daughter, Molly, ended her life after viewing harmful content online, said the codes were “overly cautious” and put tech company profit ahead of tackling harmful content.
Russell’s Molly Rose Foundation charity argues
the codes do not go far enough
to moderate suicide and self-harm content as well as blocking dangerous online challenges.
He said: “I am dismayed by the lack of ambition in today’s codes. Instead of moving fast to fix things, the painful reality is that Ofcom’s measures will fail to prevent more young deaths like my daughter Molly’s.”

data.title: Show HN: Rowboat – Open-source IDE for multi-agent systems
data.author: segmenta
data.article_summary: Rowboat是由Rowboat Labs开发的AI多智能体构建工具，利用OpenAI的Agents SDK，帮助用户在几分钟内创建多智能体工作流。用户可以通过简单的文本描述（如为食品配送公司创建助手）启动项目，并通过HTTP API或Python SDK将智能体集成到应用程序中。项目使用Docker启动，支持从本地访问。用户还可以通过API或SDK与智能体交互，实现如查询天气等功能。该工具提供详细的文档和示例代码，便于快速上手。项目遵循Apache-2.0许可证，目前在GitHub上获得654颗星和53个分支。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多代理协作系统在实际应用中的有效性及其实现方式

不同观点：
• simonw 对多代理协作的模式持怀疑态度，认为这种模式可能会使LLM代码更难获得可靠结果。他将其比作微服务架构，认为在大多数情况下，这种模式可能并不适用，只有在极少数超复杂系统中才有用。
• victorbbjorklund 引用了Open Hands项目的经验，指出在软件工程中，单个具备所有必要上下文的代理比多个代理协作更有效。他认为多代理协作的有效性尚未明确，需要更多的基准和推理来支持。
• NitpickLawyer 对该系统表示兴趣，但关注逻辑处理是否依赖于提示（prompts），并询问是否计划使用更新的库来通过代码实现更多功能，而不是简单地通过提示链希望模型能处理。

补充讨论：
• asnyder 和 flynumber 对该系统表示期待，并计划在未来试用。
• esafak 关注系统是否支持Google的A2A协议和无状态聊天。
• justanotheratom 建议在登陆页面上添加演示视频。
• sirjaz 希望该工具能以原生应用形式存在，而不是另一个web应用。
• A4ET8a8uTh0_v2 对使用案例持怀疑态度，但认为在某些项目管理场景中可能有用。
• 其他评论多为对产品外观、名称和吉祥物的轻松评价，如zcror、andsoitis、asasidh、ic_fly2等。
• whall6 提到该系统可能引发Jevon’s paradox问题。
• owebmaster 认为该系统作为一个IDE可能缺少文本编辑器。

争议焦点：
多代理协作系统在实际应用中的有效性，以及逻辑处理应通过提示还是代码实现，是主要争议点。simonw 和 victorbbjorklund 对此有不同看法，前者质疑多代理协作的实用性，后者基于实际项目经验提出了单代理的有效性。

43763967.article_summary: Rowboat是由Rowboat Labs开发的AI多智能体构建工具，利用OpenAI的Agents SDK，帮助用户在几分钟内创建多智能体工作流。用户可以通过简单的文本描述（如为食品配送公司创建助手）启动项目，并通过HTTP API或Python SDK将智能体集成到应用程序中。项目使用Docker启动，支持从本地访问。用户还可以通过API或SDK与智能体交互，实现如查询天气等功能。该工具提供详细的文档和示例代码，便于快速上手。项目遵循Apache-2.0许可证，目前在GitHub上获得654颗星和53个分支。
43763967.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多代理协作系统在实际应用中的有效性及其实现方式

不同观点：
• simonw 对多代理协作的模式持怀疑态度，认为这种模式可能会使LLM代码更难获得可靠结果。他将其比作微服务架构，认为在大多数情况下，这种模式可能并不适用，只有在极少数超复杂系统中才有用。
• victorbbjorklund 引用了Open Hands项目的经验，指出在软件工程中，单个具备所有必要上下文的代理比多个代理协作更有效。他认为多代理协作的有效性尚未明确，需要更多的基准和推理来支持。
• NitpickLawyer 对该系统表示兴趣，但关注逻辑处理是否依赖于提示（prompts），并询问是否计划使用更新的库来通过代码实现更多功能，而不是简单地通过提示链希望模型能处理。

补充讨论：
• asnyder 和 flynumber 对该系统表示期待，并计划在未来试用。
• esafak 关注系统是否支持Google的A2A协议和无状态聊天。
• justanotheratom 建议在登陆页面上添加演示视频。
• sirjaz 希望该工具能以原生应用形式存在，而不是另一个web应用。
• A4ET8a8uTh0_v2 对使用案例持怀疑态度，但认为在某些项目管理场景中可能有用。
• 其他评论多为对产品外观、名称和吉祥物的轻松评价，如zcror、andsoitis、asasidh、ic_fly2等。
• whall6 提到该系统可能引发Jevon’s paradox问题。
• owebmaster 认为该系统作为一个IDE可能缺少文本编辑器。

争议焦点：
多代理协作系统在实际应用中的有效性，以及逻辑处理应通过提示还是代码实现，是主要争议点。simonw 和 victorbbjorklund 对此有不同看法，前者质疑多代理协作的实用性，后者基于实际项目经验提出了单代理的有效性。

data.title: Can rotation solve the Hubble Puzzle?
data.author: toss1
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：宇宙是否在旋转，以及旋转的含义和相关理论

不同观点：
• est31认为宇宙中的所有物体都在旋转，包括行星、恒星、太阳系、星系和星系团，并且引用了Daly (2019) 和Pathria (1972) 的研究，提出宇宙可能具有接近最大旋转的特性，这种旋转可能源自黑洞内部的宇宙模型。
• BurningFrog质疑旋转的是时空本身，而不是宇宙中的物质，暗示对旋转主体的不同理解。
• bostonwalker提到最近一篇文章指出星系有一个优选的旋转方向，可能与宇宙本身的旋转有关，暗示宇宙旋转可能是星系旋转的原因。
• jinwoo68对宇宙旋转的相对性提出疑问，认为宇宙是唯一的整体，旋转相对什么而言？并暗示可能存在一个更大的“宇宙”。
• natch同样对旋转的相对性表示困惑。
• daxfohl分享了一个链接，视频展示了Gödel的时空穿梭解决方案中的闭合类时曲线，提供了与讨论相关的理论背景。
• hoseja强调角动量守恒，认为一切都在旋转，支持宇宙旋转的观点。
• randomcarbloke通过粗略计算，认为宇宙的旋转速度比光速边界所需的旋转速度慢一个数量级，提出对结论合理性的疑问。
• WhitneyLand对Gödel的多元贡献感到惊讶，特别是他对封闭类时曲线的发现，显示了对Gödel参与物理学讨论的意外。
• TheRealPomax对论文标题提出意见，认为标题应该总结论文内容，而非提出问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到宇宙旋转的相对性问题，特别是旋转相对什么而言，这是多个评论者（jinwoo68, natch）关注的焦点。
• 评论中引用了多项研究和理论，如Daly (2019)、Pathria (1972) 和Gödel的时空穿梭解决方案，提供了理论支持和背景信息。
• 数学计算（randomcarbloke）和物理理论（daxfohl, WhitneyLand）在讨论中扮演了重要角色，展示了定量分析和理论背景在理解宇宙旋转问题中的重要性。
• 争议的焦点在于宇宙旋转的含义和相对性问题，以及对这种旋转如何影响宇宙结构（如星系）的理解。

data.title: Show HN: Morphik – Open-source RAG that understands PDF images, runs locally
data.author: Adityav369
data.article_summary: Morphik 是一个开源的多模态 RAG（Retrieval-Augmented Generation）平台，用于在私有知识基础上构建AI应用。它支持开发者摄取、搜索（深度和浅层）、转换及管理非结构化和多模态文档，包括图像、PDF、视频等。主要功能包括多模态搜索、知识图谱构建、快速可扩展的元数据提取、与现有工具（如Google Suite、Slack等）集成，以及缓存增强生成。Morphik 提供免费 tier 并开放源码，用户可选择在线使用或自行部署。自行部署可通过直接安装或Docker进行，但开源版本不提供全面支持。此外，某些功能（如Morphik Console）仅在付费版本中提供。贡献者可通过GitHub提交错误报告、功能请求或拉取请求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源许可、功能实现、技术细节和使用反馈

不同观点：
• [codegeek] 和 [DavidPP] 提到项目的许可问题，指出某些功能（如Morphik Console和ee命名空间下的功能）并非完全遵循MIT许可，而是有不同的企业许可。这引发了对项目开源范围的讨论。
• [thot_experiment] 表达了对云服务的不信任，并询问是否存在能够本地处理私有文档并与LLM后端无关的类似项目。
• [w10-1] 对PDF处理的适用性提出疑问，尤其是对于不同类型的PDF（如会议演示文稿与学术论文）的处理是否有区别，并关注项目的测试和验证。

补充讨论：
• [mmsc] 建议通过预处理简化PDF，以提高处理效率，并提供了一个相关工具的参考。
• [trollbridge] 和 [MitPitt] 对项目的付费部分和RAG（检索增强生成）的最佳实践表示关注，尤其是对于不处理PDF的用户是否有使用价值。
• [jkc101] 关心项目的计算资源需求、扩展限制以及索引大小增长对处理速度的影响。
• [breadislove] 和 [jrvarela56] 反馈了文件上传和处理时间过长的问题，可能与系统性能或错误处理有关。
• [Alifatisk] 和 [Imanari] 询问了具体的PDF处理技术细节，如矩形提取和表格处理。
• [nostrebored] 提到ColQwen作为一个替代方案，而 [mertleee] 则好奇项目是否运行自定义LLM。

争议焦点：
• 项目许可的具体细节及其对开源范围的影响是主要争议点，尤其是企业版功能与MIT许可的区别。
• 用户对文件上传和处理的反馈显示出系统性能和错误处理方面可能存在问题。

这些观点和讨论要点反映了用户对项目功能、技术细节和使用体验的多方面关注。

Why Morphik?
-
Bug reports
Morphik is an alternative to traditional RAG for highly technical and visual documents.
Morphik
provides developers the tools to ingest, search (deep and shallow), transform, and manage unstructured and multimodal documents. Some of our features include:
Multimodal Search
: We employ techniques such as ColPali to build search that actually
understands
the visual content of documents you provide. Search over images, PDFs, videos, and more with a single endpoint.
Knowledge Graphs
: Build knowledge graphs for domain-specific use cases in a single line of code. Use our battle-tested system prompts, or use your own.
Fast and Scalable Metadata Extraction
: Extract metadata from documents - including bounding boxes, labeling, classification, and more.
Integrations
: Integrate with existing tools and workflows. Including (but not limited to) Google Suite, Slack, and Confluence.
Cache-Augmented-Generation
: Create persistent KV-caches of your documents to speed up generation.
The best part? Morphik has a
free tier
and is open source! Get started by signing up at
Morphik
.
Table of Contents
Getting Started with Morphik
Self-hosting the open-source version
Using Morphik
Contributing
Open source vs paid
Getting Started with Morphik (Recommended)
The fastest and easiest way to get started with Morphik is by signing up for free at
Morphik
. Your first 200 pages and 100 queries are on us! After this, you can pay based on usage with discounted rates for heavier use.
Self-hosting the open-source version
If you'd like to self-host Morphik, you can find the dedicated instruction
here
. We offer options for direct isntallation and installation via docker.
Important
: Due to limited resources, we cannot provide full support for open-source deployments. We have an installation guide, and a
Discord community
to help, but we can't guarantee full support.
Using Morphik
Once you've signed up for Morphik, you can get started with ingesting and search your data right away.
Code (Example: Python SDK)
For programmers, we offer a
Python SDK
and a
REST API
. Ingesting a file is as simple as:
from
morphik
import
Morphik
morphik
=
Morphik
(
"<your-morphik-uri>"
)
morphik
.
ingest_file
(
"path/to/your/super/complex/file.pdf"
)
Similarly, searching and querying your data is easy too:
morphik
.
query
(
"What's the height of screw 14-A in the chair assembly instructions?"
)
Morphik Console
You can also interact with Morphik via the Morphik Console. This is a web-based interface that allows you to ingest, search, and query your data. You can upload files, connect to different data sources, and chat with your data all within the same place.
Model Context Protocol
Finally, you can also access Morphik via MCP. Instructions are available
here
.
Contributing
You're welcome to contribute to the project! We love:
Bug reports via
GitHub issues
Feature requests via
GitHub issues
Pull requests
Currently, we're focused on improving speed, integrating with more tools, and finding the research papers that provide the most value to our users. If you ahve thoughts, let us know in the discord or in GitHub!
Open source vs paid
Certain features - such as Morphik Console - are not available in the open-source version. Any feature in the
ee
namespace is not available in the open-source version and carries a different license. Any feature outside that is open source under the MIT expat license.
Contributors
Visit our special thanks page dedicated to our contributors
here
.
PS
We took inspiration from
PostHog
while writing this README. If yo

data.title: The raccoons who made computer magazine ads great
data.author: coloneltcb
data.article_summary: 这篇文章回顾了20世纪90年代初期计算机杂志中的邮购广告，特别是PC Connection的独特广告风格。与其他充斥着产品列表和价格的枯燥广告不同，PC Connection采用由插画家Erick Ingraham创作的拟人化浣熊图像，这些图像赋予高科技产品广告一种人性化 touch。尽管这些广告的主要目的是销售电脑产品，但其温馨、富有艺术感的场景更像出自儿童读物，令人印象深刻。PC Connection凭借这些创意广告在竞争中脱颖而出，成为当时电脑邮购行业的巨头之一，尽管其总部位于新罕布什尔州的一个小镇。文章还提到，这些广告的影响力持续存在，尽管其黄金时代早已结束。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕PC Connection等老式计算机广告、艺术作品及其影响的讨论，涉及广告创意、技术发展以及对现代技术的反思。

不同观点：
• [danielvf] 强调PC Connection的出色之处在于其快速的 shipping 服务，能够在当时提供比其他邮购零售商更快捷的配送服务，这在当时是非常惊人的。
• [4ggr0] 对1984年“PC Preppy”广告中的图片表现出浓厚兴趣，并希望获得高分辨率版本，表现出对老式广告中艺术作品的欣赏。
• [BambooBandit] 指出广告中加入人物角色是为了给高科技产品增添“人性化”，并认为现代仍然需要这种做法，强调人性化在技术广告中的重要性。
• [pcdoodle] 欣赏广告中户外或窗边场景的描绘，并提到现代笔记本电脑屏幕亮度提升（1,000+ Nits）使得更好的工作和娱乐环境成为可能。
• [OJFord] 提供了更多资源链接，提到艺术家对PC Connection广告的评论，丰富了讨论内容。
• [ChrisMarshallNY] 对“MicroWarehouse Girl”的形象记忆犹新，指出其曾出现在许多杂志中，表现出对老式广告人物的怀旧。
• [cm2012] 表达了对计算机广告历史文章的喜爱。
• [agarren] 提到AST在其早期书籍封面上使用浣熊形象，质疑这种选择是否与PC广告中的浣熊有关。
• [zombot] 好奇Private Eye头戴设备的现状，认为其在当时非常先进。
• [mjevans] 对无法在archive.org或archive.today上找到当前的副本表示遗憾。
• [fullshark] 感受到对广告产生怀旧情感的认知失调。
• [rideontime] 对比2024年AI生成的浣熊与过去的艺术作品，认为AI生成的形象缺乏原作品的个性，反映出现代技术在创意表达上的不足。
• [bregma] 幽默地指出广告中的浣熊没有表现出其在现实中垃圾处理和繁殖等行为，暗示广告中的形象理想化。
• [librasteve] 提供了一个Discord链接，扩展了讨论资源。
• [sgt] 提到使用ChatGPT生成类似广告场景的尝试，指出LLM（大语言模型）对现实世界的理解不足，生成的图像不符合预期，反映了AI在理解和生成图像方面的局限性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对老式广告的怀旧情感，以及对现代技术和AI生成内容的对比和反思。
• 广告中的人物和动物形象被认为是为了增加产品的亲和力和人性化，这种策略在现代仍然被认为是有价值的。
• 讨论中还涉及了对技术发展历程的回顾，例如Private Eye头戴设备，以及对广告艺术作品的保存和获取高分辨率版本的兴趣。
• 最后，讨论还触及了AI生成内容在创意和理解方面的局限性，反映了技术进步带来的新问题和挑战。

43761633.article_content:
Do you mean to tell me you never play Microsoft Flight Simulator at your local pub? Art by Erick Ingraham from a December 1984 PC Connection ad.
When I got my first job in technology journalism, my grandmother used to call the magazine where I worked “your catalog.” I winced. But in retrospect, she wasn’t that far off. Back then, if you wanted to buy a computer product—this was the early 1990s, before the web changed everything—the odds were pretty decent that you started by buying a computer magazine.
If you remember the
computer magazines of this era
at all, you recall how thick they were—hundreds and hundreds of pages an issue in the case of the most successful ones. The majority of those pages were ads, not editorial content. And a sizable chunk of those ads were catalog-y in the extreme. Pages and pages were devoted to lists of products and prices in teensy type, with 1-800 numbers you could call to place an order.
About a gazillion mail-order houses did business this way. The April 1991
PC World
, for instance, includes advertisements for outfits such as Advanced Computer Products, Arlington Computer Products, Bulldog Computer Products, Computer Bazaar, Fast Micro, Kenosha Computer Center, NSI Computer Products, Paradise Computer Products, Telemart, and United Computer Express. Only the names and slightly varying levels of ad-design proficiency served to distinguish most of them.
But I regarded three of these companies as the industry’s giants. Whether they were the biggest, revenue-wise, I’m still not sure. It was their sustained prominence in major magazines, with multi-page spreads, that made them feel like behemoths.
One was The PC Zone, whose ads didn’t have
that
much of a distinct personality beyond a logo that vaguely evoked Rod Serling’s
The Twilight Zone
.
Most of these products are long, long gone, but a few still exist in 2025.
Then there was Micro Warehouse, best known for plastering its ads with photos of a winsome, headset-wearing sales rep named Kerry. I
think
she was a real person who actually worked there—if not, please don’t tell me.
I do hope that the NeXT computer Micro Warehouse gave away really did come with an image of Kerry.
But the crème de la mail-order crème was a company called PC Connection.
In a field where it was hard for any one merchant to stand out, PC Connection’s ads were vastly more distinctive than the competition’s. They might even one of the most memorable elements of any given issue of a magazine—yes, including the editorial material.
It wasn’t because of the portion dedicated to the business at hand. As you can see from this sample page from the October 29, 1991
PC Magazine
, that aspect of a PC Connection advertisement was not radically different from a PC Zone or Micro Warehouse ad.
The “Going back to” is the first part of a headline spread over several pages.
No, what made PC Connection ads unique was the imagery of anthropomorphic raccoons, the work of an illustrator named Erick Ingraham. Here they are in that same 1991
PC Magazine
ad.
The “Going back to” is the first part of a headline spread over several pages.
If you inspect the art closely enough, you’ll spot some boxes of vintage 1991 software, including The Microsoft Office (which, like TheFacebook.com, eventually lost its “The”). But they’re Easter eggs in a scene that is mostly about raccoons making pies—assisted by a bunny rabbit and a beaver—and playing what I assume is folk music. The piece looks like an illustration from a classy children’s book. That made sense, since Ingraham’s work in that field helped him secure his PC Connection assignment.
What on Earth was this beautifully done, homey scene—part Beatrix Potter, part Norman Rockwell—doing in a mail-order ad for computer products? The text below, by copywriter David Blistein, acknowledged that people might find it puzzling. It explained that PC Connection was based in tiny Marlow, New Hampshire (population 567) and prided itself on good customer service. The point of the characters, it said, was to add “a human touch to high tech.”
It worked. And the fact that Ingraham’s art and Blistein’s copy changed in each new ad gave magazine readers a reason to stop and pay attention. (Even Micro Warehouse’s Kerry didn’t do anything but sit there leaning on a monitor.)
The golden age of PC Connection raccoon ads began in 1983 and ended well over thirty years ago. After that, the characters retained a diminished presence in the company’s marketing into the early years of this century. Then they almost wholly vanished. They have, however, remained lodged somewhere in the back of my brain. That was true even though I caught only the tail end of their heyday. (I was
an Amiga fanatic
until 1991, and made a point of ignoring the Microsoft-centric magazines where PC Connection advertised.)
Recently, I was shocked to find that nobody has ever told the raccoons’ story. Hence this article.
Behind the scenes, PC Connection really was a small-town success story.

data.title: Revolut tracking staff behaviour with points-based 'Karma' bonus system
data.author: robaato
data.article_summary: Revolut正在使用名为"Karma"的积分系统跟踪员工行为，该系统根据员工遵守风险和合规规则的情况给予或扣除积分，最终影响奖金发放。该系统于2020年推出，积分以团队为单位汇总，集体分数用于调整个人奖金。Revolut表示，Karma系统旨在通过反馈循环奖励和纠正行为，推动积极的风险和合规实践。自实施以来，与关键风险和合规流程相关的公司整体Karma表现提高了25%。此举是Revolut改善工作文化和合规记录的一部分，以解决过去存在的会计问题、监管违规和不良工作环境等问题。Revolut去年利润增长148%至10亿英镑，主要得益于订阅收入和财富管理及加密货币交易部门的收入增加。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：团队合作与个人竞争在科技公司中的对比，特别是在金融科技环境下的合规问题

不同观点：
• Marqin认为，文中所提到的观点在团队层面很有趣。他指出，这种做法强调团队合作，而不是像许多其他科技公司那样，个人之间进行激烈的竞争。这种团队合作的方式在金融科技公司中显得独特且值得关注。

• JSR_FDED则对合规问题表达了不同的看法。他认为，尽管一开始听起来可能不太好，但这种做法实际上是针对合规问题的，对于金融公司来说是非常合理和必要的。他强调了在金融环境中合规的重要性，并暗示这种做法可能正是行业所需的。

补充讨论：
- Marqin关注的是团队合作的文化层面，强调了这种文化在科技公司中的少见和价值。
- JSR_FDED则更注重实际的功能性和行业需求，特别是合规问题在金融行业中的核心地位。
- 争议的焦点可能在于，这种以合规为导向的团队合作是否真的优于个人竞争的模式，特别是在创新和效率方面哪种模式更为有效。

Revolut says its risk- and compliance-tracking system will ‘reward and correct behaviours’.
Photograph: Dado Ruvić/Reuters
View image in fullscreen
Revolut says its risk- and compliance-tracking system will ‘reward and correct behaviours’.
Photograph: Dado Ruvić/Reuters
Revolut
Revolut tracking staff behaviour with points-based ‘Karma’ bonus system
Booming fintech company gives details of initiative to improve working culture as profits more than double
Kalyeena Makortoff
Banking correspondent
Thu 24 Apr 2025 02.00 EDT
Last modified on Thu 24 Apr 2025 03.50 EDT
Share
Revolut has been tracking staff behaviour, granting or docking points on an internal “Karma” system that is feeding into the UK bank’s decisions on bonus payouts.
The practice was detailed in Revolut’s annual report, which showed that profits had more than doubled last year, jumping by 148% to £1bn in 2024. That increase was due to a rise in subscriptions, and revenues from its wealth and crypto trading divisions.
Revolut – Europe’s most valuable fintech firm – did not disclose a bonus pool for staff, but explained that it had been building a “healthy risk and compliance culture” through a “points-based system” that was helping determine payouts for its workforce.
That system, called Karma, which launched in 2020, is used to track how well staff follow risk and compliance rules “resulting in employees gaining and losing points that will ultimately affect bonuses”, Revolut’s annual report says.
Those points are amalgamated at a team level, with their collective score then used to either dock or multiply individual employees’ final bonuses. Revolut said that Karma “serves … as a feedback loop that rewards and corrects behaviours”.
The move comes as Revolut tries to bolster a once-tarnished reputation for weak compliance and a toxic work culture. In the years after its launch in 2015, Revolut grappled with accounting issues and EU regulatory breaches, as well as
reputational concerns
, including an over-aggressive work environment, all of which are believed to have delayed the approval of its UK banking licence.
The fintech company says it has since resolved those accounting and regulatory problems, and has made efforts to
improve its working culture
.
Commenting on the programme, a Revolut spokesperson said: “Our proprietary Karma system is focused on driving positive risk and compliance actions at Revolut. This industry-leading scheme, started in 2020, effectively measures and incentivises good risk practice.
“We have seen company-wide Karma performance related to key risk and compliance processes increase by 25% since its inception, showing the success of linking these actions to remuneration, ultimately building a strong culture of risk management and compliance across the business.”
Co-founded by the former Lehman Brothers banker Nik Storonsky, Revolut originally launched as a pre-paid card focused on free currency exchange for customers. It has since grown to more than 10,000 staff, serving customers in more than 36 countries, with more than 50 products and services. As well as money transfers, it offers home rentals, buy-now pay-later credit, wage advance, e-sims, and crypto trading.

data.title: The effect of deactivating Facebook and Instagram on users' emotional state
data.author: imakwana
data.article_summary: 这篇文章通过两项大型随机实验，研究了在2020年美国大选前停用Facebook和Instagram对用户情绪状态的影响。结果显示，停用Facebook六周的用户在幸福感、抑郁和焦虑指数上提高了0.060个标准差，而停用Instagram的用户提高了0.041个标准差。进一步分析表明，Facebook的影响主要来自35岁以上人群，而Instagram的影响则主要体现在25岁以下的女性。多位作者与Meta（Facebook母公司）有经济或研究上的关联。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社交媒体对个人生活、心理健康的影响以及用户对社交媒体平台的反思和应对策略。

不同观点：
• [8s2ngy] 认为当前社交媒体的问题可以通过取消“信息流”来解决，建议只展示亲友的真实动态，而不是无关的名人或政客的内容。他支持一种更私密、小规模的社交网络。
• [donatj] 分享了自己在社交媒体（尤其是Twitter）上的失落感，认为随着用户流失和互动减少，曾经的“社交”体验已经消亡。他指出，现在的社交媒体市场不再适合那些讨论深度话题的人。
• [kleiba] 表示自己从未热衷于社交媒体，但随着孩子和家庭的社交活动越来越依赖于社交媒体（如WhatsApp），不参与可能会导致社交孤立。他对于隐私问题表示担忧，但认识到不使用社交媒体可能带来不便。
• [nomilk] 引用研究数据，认为停用Facebook和Instagram对幸福感的影响很小，质疑这些平台对心理健康的实际影响。

• [Kozmik1] 描述了家人过度使用社交媒体（如Facebook）对家庭互动的负面影响，特别是对亲密关系的影响。

• [flkiwi] 分享了自己退出Facebook和Twitter后的积极体验，但同时也提到一些家庭成员因只使用Facebook而变得“不可见”。他批评Instagram和TikTok为非真正的社交平台。

• [rimeice] 认为六周的时间不足以完全评估停用社交媒体的长期效果，建议更长的观察期。
• [Arisaka1] 指出LinkedIn上的“亮点效应”对自己求职期间的心理状态有负面影响，退出后情绪改善。
• [notepad0x90] 分享了自己仅将智能手机用于必要通信和服务的积极体验，避免内容消费，从而提高了效率和生活质量。

• 社交媒体对心理健康的实际影响存在争议，研究数据和个人体验之间存在差异。
• 不同用户对社交媒体平台的依赖程度和使用目的各异，导致各自的体验和应对策略不同。
• 停用社交媒体后，用户面临如何填补空余时间和保持社交联系的挑战。
• 隐私问题和平台的商业模式也是用户考虑退出社交媒体的重要因素。

We estimate the effect of social media deactivation on users’ emotional state in two large randomized experiments before the 2020 U.S. election. People who deactivated Facebook for the six weeks before the election reported a 0.060 standard deviation improvement in an index of happiness, depression, and anxiety, relative to controls who deactivated for just the first of those six weeks. People who deactivated Instagram for those six weeks reported a 0.041 standard deviation improvement relative to controls. Exploratory analysis suggests the Facebook effect is driven by people over 35, while the Instagram effect is driven by women under 25.

data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者对GPLv2许可证中的地址感到好奇，决定写信索取许可证副本，并最终收到GPLv3许可证的经历。GPLv2发布于1991年，当时互联网未普及，因此提供了物理地址供人们索取许可证。作者在ebay购买邮票，寄信至该地址，几周后收到回复，但发现收到的是GPLv3而非GPLv2许可证。文章反思了是否应在请求中明确提及需要GPLv2版本，并解释了因未提及具体版本而收到GPLv3的原因。最终，文章探讨了许可证历史和不同版本间的差异。

• terinjokes计划在国际旅行中尝试使用国际回信券，并对现代邮政点是否知道如何处理这些券表示好奇。

• yukiAkita认为作者的行为过于友善。
• sinuhe69开玩笑说这个故事适合“无趣人中心”这样的平台。

争议焦点：
• 邮寄信件在现代社会中的必要性和使用频率。
• GPL合规中物理地址的有效性和管理问题。
• 不同国家和地区使用不同标准的混淆。

43781888.article_content:
I wrote to the address in the GPLv2 license notice and received the GPLv3 license
Dealing with open source software, I regularly encounter many kinds of licenses — MIT, Apache, BSD, GPL being the most prominent — and I’ve taken time out to read them.  Of the many, the GNU General Public License (GPL) stands out the most.  It
reads like a letter
to the reader rather than legalese, and feels quite in tune with the spirit of open source and software freedom.
Although GPLv3 is the most current version, I commonly encounter software that makes use of GPLv2.  I got curious about the last line in its license notice:
You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
along with this program; if not, write to the Free Software
Foundation, Inc., 51 Franklin Street, Fifth Floor, Boston, MA  02110-1301, USA.
Why does this license notice have a physical address, and not a URL?  After all, even though the full license doesn’t often get included with software, it’s a simple matter to do a search and find the text of the GPLv2. Do people write to this address, and what happens if you do?
Asking the question on Stack Exchange
I turned to the
Open Source Stack Exchange
and got a very helpful answer.  It’s because the GPLv2 was published in 1991, and most people were not online.  Most people would have acquired software through physical media (such as tape or floppies) rather than a download.
Considering the storage constraints back then, it wouldn’t be surprising if developers only included the license notice, and not the entire license.  It makes sense that the most common form of communication would have been through post.
The GPLv3, published in 2007, does contain a URL in the license notice since Internet usage was more widespread at the time.
Writing to them
I decided to write to the address to see what would happen.  To do that, I would need some stamps and envelopes (I found one at my workplace) to send the request, and a self addressed enveloped with an
international reply coupon
to cover the cost of the reply.
I was disappointed to find out that the UK’s Royal Mail
discontinued international reply coupons in 2011
.  The only alternative that I could think of was to buy some US stamps.
I got some stamps
The easiest place to look for US stamps was on Ebay.  I didn’t realize that I was stepping briefly into the world of philately; most stamp listings on Ebay were covered in phrases and terminology such as very fine grade, MNH (Mint Never Hinged), FDC (First Day Cover), NDC (No Die Cut), NDN (Nondenominated), and so on.  It’s pretty easy to glean that these are properties that collectors would be looking for.
I ordered what seemed to be a ‘global’ stamp, for the smallest but safest amount that I could (about £3.86).  The listing mentioned that it was ‘uncertified’ which was mildly unnerving, did that mean it was an invalid stamp? I decided to chance it, and quickly exited that world.
After a few weeks of waiting, I eventually received the ‘African Daisy global forever vert pair’ stamp which was round!  I should have noticed that the seller sent me the item using stamps at a much lower denomination that those I had ordered.  Oh well.
Ebay seller sent me some stamps
I prepared the request
With the self addressed envelope ready, I wrote the request and addressed it to the GPLv2 address.  Luckily I did have some UK stamps available to send the letter with.
I wrote a letter
Writing the address on the envelope was awkward, as I haven’t used a pen in several years; it took a few attempts and some wasted envelopes, printing the address would have taken less time.  But it was ready so I posted it in my nearest Royal Mail box.
Receiving the reply
I had posted the letter in June 2022 and about five later weeks later, I received a reply.  The round stamps looked sufficiently stamped upon with wavy lines, known as
cancellation marks
, which are yet another thing that philatelists like to collect!
I received a reply
Anyway the letter inside contained the full license text on 5 sheets of double-sided paper.
The paper was a weird size
The first thing that came to attention, the paper that the text was printed on wasn’t an A4, it was smaller and not a size I was familiar with.  I measured it and found that it’s a US letter size paper at about 21.5cm x 27.9cm.  I completely forgot that the US, Canada, and a few other countries don’t follow the standard international paper sizes, even though I had
written about it
earlier.
I received the GPL v3
There was a problem that I noticed right away, though: this text was from the GPL
v3
, not the GPL
v2
.  In my original request I had never mentioned the GPL version I was asking about.
GPL license
The original license notice makes no mention of GPL version either.  Should the fact that the license notice contained an address have been enough metadata or a clue, that I was actually requesting the GPL v2 license? Or should I have mentioned that I was seeking the GPLv2 license?
I could

**文章主要内容：**

2025年4月23日，Hamilton Ulmer发布**Instant SQL**，这是一种新的SQL编写方式，能够在输入的同时实时更新结果集，从而加快查询构建和调试速度，无需点击运行按钮，实现零延迟。该功能现已在MotherDuck和DuckDB Local UI中预览上线。

传统SQL编写过程繁琐耗时，需要在文本编辑器中写查询、点击运行并等待结果。Instant SQL旨在解决这一问题，提供实时结果预览，让用户在输入的同时探索数据，保持分析的流畅状态。它还支持实时检查和编辑CTE（公共表表达式），并能分解复杂的列表达式，帮助用户快速定位问题。

Instant SQL不仅适用于DuckDB表，还支持MotherDuck的大表、S3的parquet文件、Postgres表、SQLite、MySQL等。它大幅提升了外部数据探索和建模的效率。此外，结合AI功能，用户可以实时预览AI编辑建议，进一步加速SQL工作流程。

总结：Instant SQL通过实时结果预览和调试，显著提升了SQL查询编写的效率和体验。

主要讨论点：DuckDB及其相关工具（如MotherDuck）的功能、优缺点以及潜在改进。

不同观点：
• **赞赏与祝贺**：
   - carlineng: 对DuckDB和MotherDuck团队在发布中的精湛工艺和创新表示赞赏，并祝贺其成功发布。
   - jwilber: 称赞MotherDuck团队的工程技艺和品味，并提到CTE预览功能对调试的帮助。

• **对管道语法的需求**：
   - motoboi: 认为DuckDB缺乏像Kusto或Google的管道查询语法，这种语法对LLM和人工编码都很有帮助，尤其在代码补全和中间结果预览方面。
   - jakozaur: 支持SQL引入管道语法，认为它能更直观地展示中间输出，并提供了一个示例说明如何改进SQL查询。

• **对功能的局限性提出质疑**：
   - jpambrun: 喜欢DuckDB的笔记本功能，但对其不能共享、导出或提交到Git repo感到限制。
   - xdkyx: 质疑DuckDB在处理复杂查询（如连接、聚合和大型表）时的性能。

• **对界面和用户体验的看法**：
   - ryguyrg: 分享了一个介绍视频链接，并对DuckDB UI和MotherDuck表示赞赏（披露自己是MotherDuck的联合创始人）。
   - hk1337: 对查询中`from`在顶部的写法表示不习惯，认为这可能只是用户偏好问题。

• **对特定功能的反馈**：
   - ayhanfuat: 认为CTE检查功能很棒，节省了大量手动操作时间。
   - almosthere: 对DuckDB的速度印象深刻，认为其现在变得更有用。
   - mritchie712: 提到DuckDB的一个有趣功能`json_serialize_sql`，并提供了示例。

• **对错误的反馈**：
   - crazygringo: 最初误解了功能，后对可视化子查询功能表示肯定。
   - potatohead24: 提到CTE选择部分经常出错，错误地选择了多个CTE。

补充讨论：
• **安全性考虑**：
   - XCSme: 希望管道语法不适用于DELETE查询，担心其潜在风险。

• **对MotherDuck的疑问**：
   - wodenokoto: 询问DuckDB UI中是否可用MotherDuck的功能，以及MotherDuck的on-prem支持情况。

争议焦点：DuckDB是否应引入像Kusto或Google的管道查询语法，以提高代码补全和中间结果预览的能力。不同用户对管道语法的便利性表示支持，但也有用户对现有SQL语法表示习惯和满意。

Instant SQL is here: Speedrun ad-hoc queries as you type
2025/04/23
-
8
min read
BY
Hamilton Ulmer
Today, we’re releasing
Instant SQL
, a new way to write SQL that updates your result set as you type to expedite query building and debugging – all with zero-latency, no run button required. Instant SQL is now available in Preview in
MotherDuck
and the
DuckDB Local UI
.
We built Instant SQL for a simple reason: writing SQL is still too tedious and slow. Not because of the language itself, but because the way we interact with databases hasn’t evolved much since SQL was created. Writing SQL isn’t just about syntax - It’s about making sense of your data, knowing what to ask, and figuring out how to get there. That process is iterative, and it’s
hard
.
"Instant SQL will save me the misery of having to try and wrangle SQL in my BI tool where iteration speed can be very slow. This lets me get the data right earlier in the process, with faster feedback than waiting for a chart to render or clearing an analytics cache."
-- Mike McClannahan, CTO,
DashFuel
Despite how much database engines have improved, with things like columnar storage, vectorized execution, and the creation of blazing-fast engines like DuckDB, which can scan billions of rows in seconds, the experience of
building
a query hasn’t kept up. We still write queries in a text editor, hit a run button, and wait to see what happens.
At MotherDuck, we've been tackling this problem from multiple angles. Last year, we released the
Column Explorer
, which gives you fast distributions and summary statistics for all the columns in your tables and result sets. We also released
FixIt
, an unreasonably effective AI fixer for SQL. MotherDuck users love these tools because they speed up data exploration and query iteration.
Instant SQL isn't just an incremental improvement to SQL tooling:
It's a fundamentally new way to interact with your queries
- one where you can see your changes instantly, debug naturally, and actually trust the code that your AI assistant suggests. No more waiting. No more context switching. Just
flow
.
Let's take a closer look at how it works.
Generate preview results as you type
Everyone knows what it feels like to start a new query from scratch. Draft, run, wait, fix, run again—an exhausting cycle that repeats hundreds of times a day.
Instant SQL gives you result set previews that update as you type. You're no longer running queries—you're exploring your data in real-time, maintaining an analytical flow state where your best thinking happens.
Whether your query is a simple transformation or a complex aggregation, Instant SQL will let you preview your results in real-time.
Inspect and edit CTEs in real-time
CTEs are easy to write, but difficult to debug. How many times a day do you comment out code to figure out what's going on in a CTE? With Instant SQL, you can now click around and instantly visualize any CTE in seconds, rather than spend hours debugging. Even better, changes you make to a CTE are immediately reflected in all dependent select nodes, giving you real-time feedback on how your modifications cascade through the query.
Break apart your complex column expressions
We've all been there; you write a complex column formula for an important business metric, and when you run the query, you get a result set full of
NULLs
. You then have to painstakingly dismantle it piece-by-piece to determine if the issue is your logic or the underlying data.
Instant SQL lets you break apart your column expressions in your
result table
to pinpoint exactly what's happening. Every edit you make to the query is instantly reflected in how data flows through the expression tree. This makes debugging anything from complex numeric formulas to regular expressions feel effortless.
Preview anything DuckDB can query - not just tables
Instant SQL works for more than just DuckDB tables; it works for massive tables in MotherDuck, parquet files in S3, Postgres tables, SQLite, MySQL, Iceberg, Delta – you name it. If DuckDB can query it, you can see a preview of it.
This is, hands down, the
best
way to quickly explore and model external data.
Fast-forward to a useful query before running it
Instant SQL gives you the freedom to test and refine your query logic without the wait. You can quickly experiment with different approaches in real-time. When you're satisfied with what you see in the preview, you can then run the query for your final, materialized results. This approach cuts hours off your SQL workflow, transforming the tedious cycle of write-run-wait into a fluid process of exploration and discovery.
Instantly preview AI-powered edit suggestions
All of these workflow improvements are great for humans, but they're even better when you throw AI features into the mix. data.title: Mark Zuckerberg Says Social Media Is Over
data.author: FinnLobsien
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了社交网络的演变以及Meta（Facebook母公司）在反垄断案中的辩护。文章指出，社交媒体曾主要是人与人之间的在线连接平台，但过去十年逐渐转向类似传统媒体，充斥着名人内容、新闻聚合和AI生成内容，个人间的社交互动减少。Meta创始人扎克伯格在反垄断审判中承认，公司已转向提供“娱乐和了解世界”的功能。数据显示，用户花在观看朋友发布内容的时间比例下降。

联邦贸易委员会（F.T.C.）指控Meta在“个人社交网络服务”行业维持非法垄断，部分通过收购Instagram和WhatsApp实现。然而，F.T.C.对社交媒体行业的定义模糊，且其反垄断案曾在2021年被驳回。Meta辩称，如今的社交媒体更像是广泛的数字内容消费，无法被单一公司垄断，并展示了与其他平台的相似性以支持其辩护。

F.T.C.的案件起源于特朗普时期，试图重新评估十多年前批准的商业交易，但证明消费者损害较为困难，因为Meta的平台均免费使用。F.T.C.认为Meta的垄断导致创新不足和消费者选择减少，但这一点也难以证实，尤其是在WhatsApp和Instagram收购时，它们尚处于早期发展阶段。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Facebook及其母公司Meta在社交媒体向内容媒体转型过程中的问题和影响

不同观点：
• **Facebook算法和内容推荐问题**：
  - **corobo**、**NullPointerWin**、**grahar64**指出，Facebook的算法导致朋友的帖子越来越少出现，取而代之的是随机的内容和广告，破坏了社交体验。用户并不是主动选择观看这些内容，而是被算法强迫观看。
  - **seydor**进一步质疑Meta展示的数据，认为用户花时间观看非朋友内容并不代表他们的真实偏好，而是算法操纵的结果。

• **Facebook的商业成功与投资者利益**：
  - **Hilift**认为Meta非常成功，每年净赚700亿美元，对投资者和广告商而言非常有利。因此，从商业角度来看，Meta的战略是成功的。

• **社交媒体的转型与用户行为变化**：
  - **throw0101d**、**jjulius**提到，Facebook从社交网络转变为内容媒体，导致用户体验从与朋友互动变为消费内容。这种变化使得社交媒体失去了原有的社交功能。
  - **curiousllama**指出，人们现在更倾向于在群聊中互动，而不是在Facebook上发布动态，这表明社交媒体的功能已经转移到其他平台。

• **Facebook对老年人和年轻人的影响**：
  - **havaloc**提到，老年用户容易受到Facebook上虚假广告的影响，缺乏应对网络安全威胁的知识。
  - **pcarolan**观察到，年轻一代更喜欢使用群聊而不是传统的社交媒体应用。

• **文化和地域差异**：
  - **Fokamul**指出，在捷克，Facebook主要被40岁以上的人用于传播政治宣传，这表明Facebook在不同地区的使用情况存在差异。

• **Meta的竞争与市场定位**：
  - **3np**认为，Meta已经从2010年代的社交媒体公司转变为与YouTube、TikTok等竞争的内容平台。尽管如此，Meta在某些市场上仍具有垄断地位。

• **社交媒体的整体衰落与健康问题**：
  - **MattDaEskimo**认为，社交媒体公司为了追求增长，忽视了用户的健康和体验，导致社交媒体成为不健康的成瘾源。
  - **Nckpz**认为，社交媒体本质上是取代了有线电视和杂志，而不是替代传统的沟通工具，用户最终会转向更高质量的沟通方式，如短信和Discord。

补充讨论：
• **朋友帖子减少的原因**：一些用户指出，朋友的帖子减少可能是因为算法的改变，导致用户错过了朋友的动态。
• **广告与用户体验的冲突**：广告的泛滥和内容的减少使得用户体验变差，这可能是社交媒体平台普遍面临的问题。
• **群聊的兴起**：有用户提到，群聊正在取代传统的社交媒体功能，成为人们分享生活的主要方式。

争议焦点：Meta是否真正理解并满足用户的需求，还是仅仅为了商业利益而改变平台性质。这涉及到用户体验与商业模式之间的平衡问题。

What, exactly, does a social network do? Is it a website that connects people with one another online, a digital gathering place where we can consume content posted by our friends? That’s certainly what it was in its heyday, in the two-thousands. Facebook was where you might find out that your friend was dating someone new, or that someone had thrown a party without inviting you. In the course of the past decade, though, social media has come to resemble something more like regular media. It’s where we find promotional videos created by celebrities, pundits shouting responses to the news, aggregated clips from pop culture, a rising tide of A.I.-generated slop, and other content designed to be broadcast to the largest number of viewers possible. The people we follow and the messages they post increasingly feel like needles in a digital haystack. Social media has become less social.
Facebook’s founder, Mark Zuckerberg, admitted as much during more than ten hours of testimony, over three days last week, in the opening phase of the Federal Trade Commission’s antitrust trial against Facebook’s parent company, Meta. The company, Zuckerberg said, has lately been involved in “the general idea of entertainment and learning about the world and discovering what’s going on.” This under-recognized shift away from interpersonal communication has been measured by the company itself. During the defense’s opening statement, Meta displayed a chart showing that the “percent of time spent viewing content posted by ‘friends’ ” has declined in the past two years, from twenty-two per cent to seventeen per cent on Facebook, and from eleven per cent to seven per cent on Instagram.
The F.T.C. is arguing that Meta maintained an illegal monopoly in the “personal social networking services” industry, in part by buying up Facebook’s competitors, such as Instagram, which the company acquired in 2012, and the messaging platform WhatsApp, which it acquired in 2014. But the F.T.C.’s definition of the social-media industry is hazy, and the antitrust case was already dismissed once, in 2021, partly because the “personal social networking services” market was too loosely defined. Meta’s counter-argument is, in a sense, that social media per se doesn’t exist now in the way that it did in the twenty-tens, and that what the company’s platforms are now known for—the digital consumption of all kinds of content—has become so widespread that no single company or platform can be said to monopolize it. In one of its slides at trial, Meta exhibited a graphic of a boxing ring showing the logos of Instagram, Facebook, and the various companies that Meta argues are competitors, including TikTok, YouTube, and Apple’s iMessage, though the F.T.C. doesn’t define any of those three as such. The company also used smartphone screenshots from the various apps to demonstrate how they’ve gravitated toward common formats: short video clips look similar on both Instagram and TikTok; messages look essentially the same in Instagram DMs as on Apple’s iMessage. Even as such similarities serve as helpful evidence for Meta’s defense, they also demonstrate how stultifying the entire online ecosystem has become. While in 2012 Facebook may have seemed singular and inescapable, now it looks like part of a crowded marketplace of apps competing to serve the same purpose.
The F.T.C.’s case, which originated during Donald Trump’s first term, entails reëvaluating business deals that it approved more than a decade ago, when the industry looked dramatically different. This makes the commission’s case less than airtight. Benedict Evans, an influential technology analyst, called the F.T.C.’s market definition of social networks “gerrymandering.” He told me, “By the F.T.C.’s definition, TikTok doesn’t compete with Facebook at all. Does that mean it would be O.K. for Facebook to buy TikTok?” Antitrust lawyers must prove that allegedly monopolistic practices cause consumer harm. In another antitrust case currently unfolding against Google, a court found that the company maintained a monopoly over parts of the online-advertising market by integrating its various automated advertising technologies, illegally privileging itself and harming its publishing customers by “reducing their revenue.” In the case of Meta, though, there is no price differential to point to—Meta’s platforms all allow users to access them for free—so the question of harm is less clear-cut.
The F.T.C. is arguing, instead, that Meta’s purported monopoly has led to a lack of innovation and to reduced consumer choice. But that, too, is difficult to prove in the case of Meta’s WhatsApp and Instagram acquisitions, because both sales occurred early in those companies’ life spans.
